title: Decredentialed jobs and upward mobility among non-college workers in the USA
title_zh: 美国非大学毕业生的去学历化工作与向上流动性
abstract: Prominent employers are increasingly dropping college degree requirements when hiring. Does this provide upward mobility for non-college workers? Matching job postings to 446,500 job starts in US administrative data from 2011 to 2021, we show that employers reduced the share of postings requiring a degree by more than 10%. Non-college workers who move to decredentialed jobs earn 12 log points more than matched workers moving to never-credentialed jobs (β = 0.124; 95% confidence interval, (0.042, 0.206)), around US$4,600 per year—a premium that endures for at least five years. These hires are more likely to be Black, Hispanic and female than the workers they replace. Employers also benefit, as removing degree requirements reduces labour costs. Yet most employers that drop requirements do not hire non-college workers (non-college hiring rises 1.2 percentage points; 95% confidence interval, (0.5, 2.0)). Decredentialing is a promising tool for social mobility, but only when employers follow through. Linking job postings to US Census earnings records from 2011 to 2021, Lyttelton et al. find that non-college workers hired into jobs that dropped degree requirements earned around US$4,600 more per year, yet employers rarely hired non-college workers after decredentialing.
abstract_zh: 越来越多的知名雇主在招聘时取消了大学学位要求。这对非大学毕业生的向上流动有何影响？研究人员将2011年至2021年间的美国行政数据中446,500个工作起点与职位招聘信息相匹配，显示雇主将要求学位的职位比例降低了10%以上。与转入从未要求学位的职位相比，转入去学历化职位的非大学毕业生年收入提高12个百分点（β = 0.124；95%置信区间，(0.042, 0.206)），约每年4,600美元——这一溢价至少持续五年。这些新进员工比他们替代的工人更有可能是黑人、西班牙裔和女性。雇主也受益，因为取消学位要求降低了劳动力成本。然而，大多数取消学历要求的雇主并未雇佣非大学毕业生（非大学毕业生的招聘比例上升1.2个百分点；95%置信区间，(0.5, 2.0)）。去学历化是促进社会流动的有前景的工具，但仅当雇主真正执行时才有效。利用2011年至2021年的美国人口普查收入记录将职位招聘信息与数据相连接，Lyttelton等人发现，被雇用到取消学历要求的职位的非大学毕业生每年收入约多4,600美元，然而雇主在去学历化后很少雇佣非大学毕业生。
